Access export of an invented code hosting service. The rules in this export decide every request.

Access rules (they apply exactly as written):
1. Each assignment names a role and either a user or a group. If it names a group, exactly the users listed as members of that group hold the role.
2. Assignments reach downward only: the namespace where an assignment is made and everything below it, however deep, are covered; namespaces beside it or above it are not.
3. The actions a role allows are the ones listed for that role.
4. The inclusion list says which action includes which. If X includes Y, a role that allows X allows Y as well; inclusions chain, so if Y in turn includes Z, then X includes Z. Only the listed inclusions exist, and none works in reverse.

state.policy:
Refund policy

General provisions
- In a conflict between rules, the earlier rule in the list prevails.
- By default a request is denied unless a rule says otherwise.

Rules
(1) When the time since purchase is under 30 days and the record shows yes for the proof of purchase flag: Approve the request.
(2) When the refund amount exceeds 300 EUR and the time since purchase is not below 30 days and the number of earlier refunds is at least 3: Escalate the request to a human reviewer.
(3) When the account age is lower than 14 days and the record shows yes for the fraud alert flag: Deny the request.
(4) When the time since purchase is greater than 21 days: Escalate the request to a human reviewer.
(5) When the account age is at least 120 days and the fraud alert flag is set to no: Approve the request.
(6) When the number of earlier refunds exceeds 4 and the refund amount is at least 1500 EUR: Deny the request.
(7) When the fraud alert flag is set to yes and the record shows no for the proof of purchase flag: Escalate the request to a human reviewer.
(8) When the time since purchase is 45 days or less and the number of earlier refunds is less than 2 and the record shows no for the fraud alert flag: Approve the request.
(9) When the fraud alert flag is set to yes and the number of earlier refunds is 4 or higher and the region is either Jordor or Yarvik: Deny the request.
(10) When the time since purchase is more than 21 days and the refund amount is at least 400 EUR: Deny the request.
(11) When the proof of purchase flag is no and the region is none of Galxan or Corwick and the refund amount is between 300 and 1500 EUR inclusive: Escalate the request to a human reviewer.
(12) When the case has the proof of purchase flag set to yes and the refund amount is below 200 EUR: Approve the request.

Exceptions
- Rule 8 is waived if the case has the proof of purchase flag set to no.
- Rule 9 is waived if the time since purchase is below 21 days.
- Rule 7 is waived if the refund amount is 400 EUR or less.
- Rule 4 is waived if the account age is 90 days or more and the case has the fraud alert flag set to no.

- class: the triage class (1 = most urgent)
- arrived: time the patient arrived (today, 24-hour clock)
- flag: a marker noted for the patient; "-" means no marker
- slot: time of the booked slot, "-" if there is none
- consult: expected consultation time in minutes

The order is fixed by these rules, taken in the order given:
1. Waiting at least 25 minutes lifts a patient by one class.
2. Any patient carrying the flag "infant" is lifted by one class.
3. The patients are taken class by class, smallest class number first.
4. Inside a class, every patient whose booked slot is due precedes every patient whose booked slot is not due.
5. Lower ticket number first.

Notes on the rules:
- Read the rules from top to bottom; a later rule is used only to separate patients that every earlier rule leaves level.
- Rules 1 and 2 do not order anything by themselves: they set the class that the later rules use.
- A patient that moves up one class gets the next smaller class number, for instance 3 instead of 4.
- No patient can go higher than class 1; a patient of class 1 stays in class 1 whatever applies to it.
- After a class change a patient is treated like every other patient of its new class.
- To get the waiting time, subtract the "arrived" time from the current time (in minutes; same day; 24-hour clock).
- A wait of exactly 25 minutes counts as at least 25 minutes.
- Both class changes can apply to the same patient; it then moves up two classes in total, stopping at class 1.
- A booked slot counts as due from its own minute on, that is, when it is not later than the current time.
- The patients with a due booked slot are level with each other under this rule (the times under "slot" are not compared), and so are the patients without a due one.
- Rank every waiting patient once, as things stand at the current time; the position asked for is a place in that ranking.
- Only what the rules name counts; any other column or flag changes nothing.
- Every patient has its own ticket number: the number that follows the dash in the identifier.

Rule 5. When the number of exports in the last 30 days is 1 or less: Approve the request.

- If the export size is above 1000 records, Rule 6 does not apply.
- If the account age is less than 30 days and the record shows no for the consent on file flag, Rule 5 does not apply.
- If the account age is under 30 days, Rule 1 does not apply.
- If the number of exports in the last 30 days does not exceed 1 and the export size does not exceed 5000 records, Rule 3 does not apply.

How each kind of step works:
  set: the file at the path gets the given content (a new file if there was none, otherwise the old content is overwritten).
  delete: the file at the path is gone afterwards.
  rename: new name, same folder; when the new name is taken, the other file is replaced.
  copy: the destination path receives the source's content (replacing any file there); the source is not changed.
  move: relocates the file to the folder, keeping its file name; an existing file with that name in the folder is overwritten.

state:
A pipeline runner called mipula-27 is to receive plugins from the plugin registry.

How to read the entries and when a set is clean:
* To order two versions, compare the first numbers, then the second, then the third, always as whole numbers, so 0.10.1 comes after 0.9.8 and 1.2.10 after 1.2.9. The same holds for the two-part runtime versions: 2.10 comes after 2.9.
* Bounds read as follows: >= at least, > strictly newer, <= at most, < strictly older, == exactly this version, != anything but this version; where several bounds follow one name, all of them apply.
* The proposed set installs cleanly when every pinned version is listed in the plugin registry, every requirement of every pinned version names a plugin that is pinned at a version meeting all of its bounds, the runtime of the target environment meets every runtime bound of every pinned version, and no conflict entry of a pinned version applies to another pin.
* Entries of versions that are not pinned are irrelevant.
* No plugin is added automatically: if a pinned version requires a plugin that has no pin, that requirement fails.
* Pinning a plugin that nothing needs is allowed, but the entry of that pinned version must still be met.
* Runtime bounds are checked against the runtime of the target environment; a version marked 'any' runs on every runtime.
* If a pinned version has a 'conflicts with' entry naming another plugin and that plugin is pinned at a version inside the given bound, the set is not clean (whichever side lists it); entries about plugins that are not pinned, or whose pin lies outside the bound, are harmless.

state:
Proposed install on ostrvar-24, a game server: the extensions pinned at the end, taken from the extension catalogue below.

Rules of this check:
* To order two versions, compare the first numbers, then the second, then the third, always as whole numbers, so 0.10.1 comes after 0.9.8 and 1.2.10 after 1.2.9. The same holds for the two-part runtime versions: 2.10 comes after 2.9.
* After an extension name come one or more bounds separated by commas, and every bound must hold: >=V at least V, >V newer than V, <=V at most V, <V older than V, ==V exactly V, !=V any version except V.
* The set is clean only if the extension catalogue lists every pinned version, every requirement of a pinned version is met by the pin of the required extension, each runtime bound of a pinned version holds for the environment's runtime, and none of the pinned versions has a conflict entry that applies to another pin.
* Only the entries of the pinned versions count; what the extension catalogue says about other versions plays no part.
* Only pinned extensions get installed; a required extension that has no pin counts as unmet.
* A pin that no pinned version requires does no harm by itself; its own entry is checked like that of every other pin.
* Runtime bounds are checked against the runtime of the target environment; a version marked 'any' runs on every runtime.
* If a pinned version has a 'cannot be combined with' entry naming another extension and that extension is pinned at a version inside the given bound, the set is not clean (whichever side lists it); entries about extensions that are not pinned, or whose pin lies outside the bound, are harmless.

state:
Proposed install on sarnilo-45, a pipeline runner: the plugins pinned at the end, taken from the plugin registry below.

Rules of this check:
* Versions are ordered part by part as integers, not as text: 3.10.0 is later than 3.9.9, and 2.0.0 is later than 1.15.2. Runtime versions (two parts) follow the same order, so 4.11 is later than 4.9.
* Bounds read as follows: >= at least, > strictly newer, <= at most, < strictly older, == exactly this version, != anything but this version; where several bounds follow one name, all of them apply.
* The proposed set installs cleanly when every pinned version is listed in the plugin registry, every requirement of every pinned version names a plugin that is pinned at a version meeting all of its bounds, the runtime of the target environment meets every runtime bound of every pinned version, and no conflict entry of a pinned version applies to another pin.
* Entries of versions that are not pinned are irrelevant.
* No plugin is added automatically: if a pinned version requires a plugin that has no pin, that requirement fails.
* Pinning a plugin that nothing needs is allowed, but the entry of that pinned version must still be met.
* The environment's runtime must satisfy each runtime bound of each pinned version ('any' means no bound).
* An entry 'clashes with P B' under a pinned version means that the set fails when P is pinned at a version meeting the bound B; it does not matter which of the two lists it, and an entry about a plugin without a pin, or whose pin misses B, does no harm.

state:
A pipeline runner called virnrin-15 is to receive plugins from the plugin registry.

Rules of this check:
* Versions are compared number by number from the left, each number as a whole number: 1.10.0 is newer than 1.9.3, and 2.0.0 is newer than 1.12.7. Runtime versions (two parts) follow the same order, so 4.11 is later than 4.9.
* Each bound is an operator and a version: >= (that version or newer), > (newer only), <= (that version or older), < (older only), == (only that version), != (every version but that one); a list of bounds is met only when each bound is met.
* A clean install needs all of the following: each pin is a version that the plugin registry lists; for each pinned version, each plugin it depends on is pinned too, at a version inside the stated bounds; the runtime of the environment satisfies the runtime bounds of all pinned versions; no pinned version has a 'conflicts with' entry that applies to another pin.
* Only the entries of the pinned versions count; what the plugin registry says about other versions plays no part.
* Only pinned plugins get installed; a required plugin that has no pin counts as unmet.
* Pinning a plugin that nothing needs is allowed, but the entry of that pinned version must still be met.
* A runtime bound of a pinned version is met when the runtime of the target environment satisfies it; 'any' sets no runtime bound.
* An entry 'conflicts with P B' under a pinned version means that the set fails when P is pinned at a version meeting the bound B; it does not matter which of the two lists it, and an entry about a plugin without a pin, or whose pin misses B, does no harm.

state:
sarneth-01 (a robot controller) should get the components listed under the pins, drawn from the component depot.

How to read the entries and when a set is clean:
* To order two versions, compare the first numbers, then the second, then the third, always as whole numbers, so 0.10.1 comes after 0.9.8 and 1.2.10 after 1.2.9. Runtime versions (two parts) follow the same order, so 4.11 is later than 4.9.
* Bounds read as follows: >= at least, > strictly newer, <= at most, < strictly older, == exactly this version, != anything but this version; where several bounds follow one name, all of them apply.
* A clean install needs all of the following: each pin is a version that the component depot lists; for each pinned version, each component it needs is pinned too, at a version inside the stated bounds; the runtime of the environment satisfies the runtime bounds of all pinned versions; no pinned version has a 'cannot be combined with' entry that applies to another pin.
* Only the entries of the pinned versions count; what the component depot says about other versions plays no part.
* Only pinned components get installed; a required component that has no pin counts as unmet.
* Extra pins are fine: a pinned component that nothing requires is harmless as long as its own entry is satisfied.
* A runtime bound of a pinned version is met when the runtime of the target environment satisfies it; 'any' sets no runtime bound.
* If a pinned version has a 'cannot be combined with' entry naming another component and that component is pinned at a version inside the given bound, the set is not clean (whichever side lists it); entries about components that are not pinned, or whose pin lies outside the bound, are harmless.

state.policy:
Refund approval policy

General provisions
- Conflicting rules are resolved in favour of the rule with the larger number.
- When none of the rules applies, approve the request.

Rules
1. A request for which the time since purchase is 45 days or more is denied.
2. A request for which the time since purchase is more than 90 days and the number of earlier refunds is 2 or higher is escalated to a human reviewer.
3. A request for which the fraud alert flag is no is approved.
4. A request for which the number of earlier refunds is at least 3 and the account age is not more than 180 days is escalated to a human reviewer.
5. A request for which the proof of purchase flag is set to no is denied.
6. A request for which the bank dispute flag is set to yes and the time since purchase is more than 21 days is escalated to a human reviewer.
7. A request for which the number of earlier refunds is less than 2 and the region is either Talxan or Kelmun and the time since purchase is not more than 45 days is approved.
8. A request for which the case has the bank dispute flag set to yes and the fraud alert flag is set to yes and the account age is 270 days or less is escalated to a human reviewer.
9. A request for which the bank dispute flag is yes and the record shows yes for the fraud alert flag and the account age does not exceed 60 days is denied.
10. A request for which the bank dispute flag is set to yes and the number of earlier refunds is within 2 to 4 with both limits included is denied.
11. A request for which the bank dispute flag is no and the account age is more than 270 days is approved.
12. A request for which the time since purchase is lower than 14 days and the account age is 180 days or higher is approved.

Exceptions
- Rule 7 does not apply when the case has the fraud alert flag set to yes.
- Rule 1 does not apply when the number of earlier refunds is lower than 1.
- Rule 8 does not apply when the proof of purchase flag is yes and the number of earlier refunds is lower than 2.
- Rule 6 does not apply when the record shows yes for the proof of purchase flag and the fraud alert flag is no.

lermaro-42 (a robot controller) should get the components listed under the pins, drawn from the component depot.

How to read the entries and when a set is clean:
- To order two versions, compare the first numbers, then the second, then the third, always as whole numbers, so 0.10.1 comes after 0.9.8 and 1.2.10 after 1.2.9. Runtime versions (two parts) follow the same order, so 4.11 is later than 4.9.
- Each bound is an operator and a version: >= (that version or newer), > (newer only), <= (that version or older), < (older only), == (only that version), != (every version but that one); a list of bounds is met only when each bound is met.
- The set is clean only if the component depot lists every pinned version, every requirement of a pinned version is met by the pin of the required component, each runtime bound of a pinned version holds for the environment's runtime, and none of the pinned versions has a conflict entry that applies to another pin.
- Entries of versions that are not pinned are irrelevant.
- No component is added automatically: if a pinned version requires a component that has no pin, that requirement fails.
- A pin that no pinned version requires does no harm by itself; its own entry is checked like that of every other pin.
- The environment's runtime must satisfy each runtime bound of each pinned version ('any' means no bound).
- An entry 'clashes with P B' under a pinned version means that the set fails when P is pinned at a version meeting the bound B; it does not matter which of the two lists it, and an entry about a component without a pin, or whose pin misses B, does no harm.

Proposed install on nuvurn-12, a field controller: the modules pinned at the end, taken from the module feed below.

Conventions:
* To order two versions, compare the first numbers, then the second, then the third, always as whole numbers, so 0.10.1 comes after 0.9.8 and 1.2.10 after 1.2.9. Runtime versions (two parts) follow the same order, so 4.11 is later than 4.9.
* Bounds read as follows: >= at least, > strictly newer, <= at most, < strictly older, == exactly this version, != anything but this version; where several bounds follow one name, all of them apply.
* The set is clean only if the module feed lists every pinned version, every requirement of a pinned version is met by the pin of the required module, each runtime bound of a pinned version holds for the environment's runtime, and none of the pinned versions has a conflict entry that applies to another pin.
* Requirements and other entries of versions without a pin do not matter.
* No module is added automatically: if a pinned version requires a module that has no pin, that requirement fails.
* Pinning a module that nothing needs is allowed, but the entry of that pinned version must still be met.
* The environment's runtime must satisfy each runtime bound of each pinned version ('any' means no bound).
* An entry 'conflicts with P B' under a pinned version means that the set fails when P is pinned at a version meeting the bound B; it does not matter which of the two lists it, and an entry about a module without a pin, or whose pin misses B, does no harm.

An analysis workstation called rukenk-20 is to receive packages from the package index.

Rules of this check:
1. Versions are ordered part by part as integers, not as text: 3.10.0 is later than 3.9.9, and 2.0.0 is later than 1.15.2. The same holds for the two-part runtime versions: 2.10 comes after 2.9.
2. Bounds read as follows: >= at least, > strictly newer, <= at most, < strictly older, == exactly this version, != anything but this version; where several bounds follow one name, all of them apply.
3. A clean install needs all of the following: each pin is a version that the package index lists; for each pinned version, each package it requires is pinned too, at a version inside the stated bounds; the runtime of the environment satisfies the runtime bounds of all pinned versions; no pinned version has a 'cannot be combined with' entry that applies to another pin.
4. Only the entries of the pinned versions count; what the package index says about other versions plays no part.
5. No package is added automatically: if a pinned version requires a package that has no pin, that requirement fails.
6. Extra pins are fine: a pinned package that nothing requires is harmless as long as its own entry is satisfied.
7. The environment's runtime must satisfy each runtime bound of each pinned version ('any' means no bound).
8. Conflicts ('cannot be combined with'): a pinned version that names a package P with a bound blocks the set exactly when P is pinned at a version meeting that bound; if P has no pin, or its pin misses the bound, nothing happens.

How to read the entries and when a set is clean:
1. Versions are ordered part by part as integers, not as text: 3.10.0 is later than 3.9.9, and 2.0.0 is later than 1.15.2. The same holds for the two-part runtime versions: 2.10 comes after 2.9.
2. Bounds read as follows: >= at least, > strictly newer, <= at most, < strictly older, == exactly this version, != anything but this version; where several bounds follow one name, all of them apply.
3. The proposed set installs cleanly when every pinned version is listed in the package index, every requirement of every pinned version names a package that is pinned at a version meeting all of its bounds, the runtime of the target environment meets every runtime bound of every pinned version, and no conflict entry of a pinned version applies to another pin.
4. Only the entries of the pinned versions count; what the package index says about other versions plays no part.
5. No package is added automatically: if a pinned version requires a package that has no pin, that requirement fails.
6. A pin that no pinned version requires does no harm by itself; its own entry is checked like that of every other pin.
7. A runtime bound of a pinned version is met when the runtime of the target environment satisfies it; 'any' sets no runtime bound.
8. If a pinned version has a 'cannot be combined with' entry naming another package and that package is pinned at a version inside the given bound, the set is not clean (whichever side lists it); entries about packages that are not pinned, or whose pin lies outside the bound, are harmless.

state:
Proposed install on zartem-06, a field controller: the modules pinned at the end, taken from the module feed below.

How to read the entries and when a set is clean:
- Versions are ordered part by part as integers, not as text: 3.10.0 is later than 3.9.9, and 2.0.0 is later than 1.15.2. Runtime versions (two parts) follow the same order, so 4.11 is later than 4.9.
- Each bound is an operator and a version: >= (that version or newer), > (newer only), <= (that version or older), < (older only), == (only that version), != (every version but that one); a list of bounds is met only when each bound is met.
- The set is clean only if the module feed lists every pinned version, every requirement of a pinned version is met by the pin of the required module, each runtime bound of a pinned version holds for the environment's runtime, and none of the pinned versions has a conflict entry that applies to another pin.
- Only the entries of the pinned versions count; what the module feed says about other versions plays no part.
- No module is added automatically: if a pinned version requires a module that has no pin, that requirement fails.
- A pin that no pinned version requires does no harm by itself; its own entry is checked like that of every other pin.
- A runtime bound of a pinned version is met when the runtime of the target environment satisfies it; 'any' sets no runtime bound.
- An entry 'cannot be combined with P B' under a pinned version means that the set fails when P is pinned at a version meeting the bound B; it does not matter which of the two lists it, and an entry about a module without a pin, or whose pin misses B, does no harm.

A game server called peskvar-39 is to receive extensions from the extension catalogue.

Conventions:
1. Versions are compared number by number from the left, each number as a whole number: 1.10.0 is newer than 1.9.3, and 2.0.0 is newer than 1.12.7. Runtime versions (two parts) follow the same order, so 4.11 is later than 4.9.
2. Each bound is an operator and a version: >= (that version or newer), > (newer only), <= (that version or older), < (older only), == (only that version), != (every version but that one); a list of bounds is met only when each bound is met.
3. The set is clean only if the extension catalogue lists every pinned version, every requirement of a pinned version is met by the pin of the required extension, each runtime bound of a pinned version holds for the environment's runtime, and none of the pinned versions has a conflict entry that applies to another pin.
4. Requirements and other entries of versions without a pin do not matter.
5. Only pinned extensions get installed; a required extension that has no pin counts as unmet.
6. Pinning an extension that nothing needs is allowed, but the entry of that pinned version must still be met.
7. A runtime bound of a pinned version is met when the runtime of the target environment satisfies it; 'any' sets no runtime bound.
8. An entry 'clashes with P B' under a pinned version means that the set fails when P is pinned at a version meeting the bound B; it does not matter which of the two lists it, and an entry about an extension without a pin, or whose pin misses B, does no harm.

Proposed install on sarnryx-16, an analysis workstation: the packages pinned at the end, taken from the package index below.

Conventions:
1. To order two versions, compare the first numbers, then the second, then the third, always as whole numbers, so 0.10.1 comes after 0.9.8 and 1.2.10 after 1.2.9. Runtime versions (two parts) follow the same order, so 4.11 is later than 4.9.
2. Each bound is an operator and a version: >= (that version or newer), > (newer only), <= (that version or older), < (older only), == (only that version), != (every version but that one); a list of bounds is met only when each bound is met.
3. A clean install needs all of the following: each pin is a version that the package index lists; for each pinned version, each package it needs is pinned too, at a version inside the stated bounds; the runtime of the environment satisfies the runtime bounds of all pinned versions; no pinned version has a 'conflicts with' entry that applies to another pin.
4. Entries of versions that are not pinned are irrelevant.
5. Only pinned packages get installed; a required package that has no pin counts as unmet.
6. Pinning a package that nothing needs is allowed, but the entry of that pinned version must still be met.
7. A runtime bound of a pinned version is met when the runtime of the target environment satisfies it; 'any' sets no runtime bound.
8. An entry 'conflicts with P B' under a pinned version means that the set fails when P is pinned at a version meeting the bound B; it does not matter which of the two lists it, and an entry about a package without a pin, or whose pin misses B, does no harm.

8. If a pinned version has a 'clashes with' entry naming another extension and that extension is pinned at a version inside the given bound, the set is not clean (whichever side lists it); entries about extensions that are not pinned, or whose pin lies outside the bound, are harmless.

A game server called ostrvek-14 is to receive extensions from the extension catalogue.

Conventions:

* Bounds read as follows: >= at least, > strictly newer, <= at most, < strictly older, == exactly this version, != anything but this version; where several bounds follow one name, all of them apply.
* A clean install needs all of the following: each pin is a version that the extension catalogue lists; for each pinned version, each extension it depends on is pinned too, at a version inside the stated bounds; the runtime of the environment satisfies the runtime bounds of all pinned versions; no pinned version has a 'cannot be combined with' entry that applies to another pin.

* Runtime bounds are checked against the runtime of the target environment; a version marked 'any' runs on every runtime.
* If a pinned version has a 'cannot be combined with' entry naming another extension and that extension is pinned at a version inside the given bound, the set is not clean (whichever side lists it); entries about extensions that are not pinned, or whose pin lies outside the bound, are harmless.

state:
Permission data of a fictional records system, followed by the rules that govern it.

Request under review: t.nirzelt wants to lookup on section vehicles-open.

How access is decided:
1. A role is held by the user an assignment names or, when it names a group, by every member of that group. The members of a group are the users on its list plus all members of each group on its list, and so on through further nesting. A group that is nested inside another gains no members from the group that contains it.
2. Assignments reach downward only: the section where an assignment is made and everything below it, however deep, are covered; sections beside it or above it are not.
3. A sealed section blocks assignments from above: an assignment made at a higher section covers neither the sealed section nor anything below it. An assignment made at the sealed section itself, or at a section below it, is not affected by that seal, and sections outside the sealed section are not affected either.
4. A role allows the actions listed for it. A role that extends another role also allows everything the other role allows, including what that role gets from a role it extends. Extension works one way only: the extended role gains nothing.
5. The inclusion list says which action includes which. If X includes Y, a role that allows X allows Y as well; inclusions chain, so if Y in turn includes Z, then X includes Z. Only the listed inclusions exist, and none works in reverse.
6. Deny entries win over assignments. An entry blocks its action for the user it names, or for every member of the group it names (members through nested groups included), on its section and on everything below that section, sealed or not. It blocks that single action only; requests for other actions are judged as if the entry were not there, also when the actions are linked by an inclusion.
7. A request is allowed only when an assignment whose role the requester holds covers the requested section and that role allows the requested action; in addition no deny entry may apply.

rukgan-40 (a pipeline runner) should get the plugins listed under the pins, drawn from the plugin registry.

Rules of this check:
* Versions are compared number by number from the left, each number as a whole number: 1.10.0 is newer than 1.9.3, and 2.0.0 is newer than 1.12.7. The same holds for the two-part runtime versions: 2.10 comes after 2.9.
* Bounds read as follows: >= at least, > strictly newer, <= at most, < strictly older, == exactly this version, != anything but this version; where several bounds follow one name, all of them apply.
* The set is clean only if the plugin registry lists every pinned version, every requirement of a pinned version is met by the pin of the required plugin, each runtime bound of a pinned version holds for the environment's runtime, and none of the pinned versions has a conflict entry that applies to another pin.
* Only the entries of the pinned versions count; what the plugin registry says about other versions plays no part.
* No plugin is added automatically: if a pinned version requires a plugin that has no pin, that requirement fails.
* Extra pins are fine: a pinned plugin that nothing requires is harmless as long as its own entry is satisfied.
* The environment's runtime must satisfy each runtime bound of each pinned version ('any' means no bound).
* An entry 'cannot be combined with P B' under a pinned version means that the set fails when P is pinned at a version meeting the bound B; it does not matter which of the two lists it, and an entry about a plugin without a pin, or whose pin misses B, does no harm.

GENERAL

state:
Permission data of a fictional code hosting service, followed by the rules that govern it.

Request: user w.droltegh asks to release at the namespace ingest.

Access rules (they apply exactly as written):
1. An assignment gives one role to one user or to one group. An assignment to a group counts for every member of the group. Membership passes through nested groups: when group X is listed as a member of group Y, all members of X (also those X has through its own nested groups) are members of Y. It does not pass the other way: a user listed directly in Y is not thereby a member of X.
2. Assignments reach downward only: the namespace where an assignment is made and everything below it, however deep, are covered; namespaces beside it or above it are not.
3. Exception for sealed namespaces: an assignment never passes into a sealed namespace from a namespace above it, so the sealed namespace and everything below it stay out of its reach. A seal does nothing to an assignment made at the sealed namespace or below it, and nothing to namespaces that are not inside the sealed namespace.
4. The actions a role allows are its own actions plus the actions of the role it extends, plus those of the role that one extends, and so on. Nothing is passed in the opposite direction, from the extending role to the extended one.
5. The inclusion list says which action includes which. If X includes Y, a role that allows X allows Y as well; inclusions chain, so if Y in turn includes Z, then X includes Z. Only the listed inclusions exist, and none works in reverse.
6. Decision: a request is allowed when some assignment that counts for the requester covers the requested namespace with a role that allows the requested action. In every other case it is not allowed.

Data export policy

Rule 6. A request for which the number of exports in the last 30 days is within 2 to 3 with both limits included and the account age is under 60 days is denied.

Rule 12. A request for which the verified requester flag is yes and the legal hold flag is set to no is approved.

state:
A pipeline runner called virnrin-15 is to receive plugins from the plugin registry.

Rules of this check:
* Versions are compared number by number from the left, each number as a whole number: 1.10.0 is newer than 1.9.3, and 2.0.0 is newer than 1.12.7. Runtime versions (two parts) follow the same order, so 4.11 is later than 4.9.
* Each bound is an operator and a version: >= (that version or newer), > (newer only), <= (that version or older), < (older only), == (only that version), != (every version but that one); a list of bounds is met only when each bound is met.
* A clean install needs all of the following: each pin is a version that the plugin registry lists; for each pinned version, each plugin it depends on is pinned too, at a version inside the stated bounds; the runtime of the environment satisfies the runtime bounds of all pinned versions; no pinned version has a 'conflicts with' entry that applies to another pin.
* Only the entries of the pinned versions count; what the plugin registry says about other versions plays no part.
* Only pinned plugins get installed; a required plugin that has no pin counts as unmet.
* Pinning a plugin that nothing needs is allowed, but the entry of that pinned version must still be met.
* A runtime bound of a pinned version is met when the runtime of the target environment satisfies it; 'any' sets no runtime bound.
* An entry 'conflicts with P B' under a pinned version means that the set fails when P is pinned at a version meeting the bound B; it does not matter which of the two lists it, and an entry about a plugin without a pin, or whose pin misses B, does no harm.

state:
Permission data of a fictional code hosting service, followed by the rules that govern it.

Request under review: p.serkogh wants to comment on namespace legacy-app.

How access is decided:
- A role is held by the user an assignment names or, when the assignment names a group, by each user listed in that group. Users who are not listed in the group get nothing from it.
- An assignment is made at one namespace. It covers that namespace and every namespace below it (directly or further down), and nothing else.
- The actions a role allows are the ones listed for that role.
- The inclusion list says which action includes which. If X includes Y, a role that allows X allows Y as well; inclusions chain, so if Y in turn includes Z, then X includes Z. Only the listed inclusions exist, and none works in reverse.
- Decision: a request is allowed when some assignment that counts for the requester covers the requested namespace with a role that allows the requested action. In every other case it is not allowed.

state:
Proposed install on yegryx-12, a pipeline runner: the plugins pinned at the end, taken from the plugin registry below.

Conventions:
- To order two versions, compare the first numbers, then the second, then the third, always as whole numbers, so 0.10.1 comes after 0.9.8 and 1.2.10 after 1.2.9. Runtime versions have two numbers and are compared the same way (3.10 is newer than 3.9).
- Each bound is an operator and a version: >= (that version or newer), > (newer only), <= (that version or older), < (older only), == (only that version), != (every version but that one); a list of bounds is met only when each bound is met.
- A clean install needs all of the following: each pin is a version that the plugin registry lists; for each pinned version, each plugin it depends on is pinned too, at a version inside the stated bounds; the runtime of the environment satisfies the runtime bounds of all pinned versions; no pinned version has a 'clashes with' entry that applies to another pin.
- Requirements and other entries of versions without a pin do not matter.
- No plugin is added automatically: if a pinned version requires a plugin that has no pin, that requirement fails.
- Pinning a plugin that nothing needs is allowed, but the entry of that pinned version must still be met.
- A runtime bound of a pinned version is met when the runtime of the target environment satisfies it; 'any' sets no runtime bound.
- If a pinned version has a 'clashes with' entry naming another plugin and that plugin is pinned at a version inside the given bound, the set is not clean (whichever side lists it); entries about plugins that are not pinned, or whose pin lies outside the bound, are harmless.

Permission data of a fictional code hosting service, followed by the rules that govern it.

Request: user w.droltegh asks to release at the namespace ingest.

Access rules (they apply exactly as written):
1. An assignment gives one role to one user or to one group. An assignment to a group counts for every member of the group. Membership passes through nested groups: when group X is listed as a member of group Y, all members of X (also those X has through its own nested groups) are members of Y. It does not pass the other way: a user listed directly in Y is not thereby a member of X.
2. Assignments reach downward only: the namespace where an assignment is made and everything below it, however deep, are covered; namespaces beside it or above it are not.

state.policy:
Data export policy

RULES
1. A request for which the export size is greater than 10000 records and the legal hold flag is set to yes and the record shows yes for the personal data flag is denied.
2. A request for which the export size is 50000 records or higher is escalated to a human reviewer.
3. A request for which the verified requester flag is set to no is denied.
4. A request for which the number of exports in the last 30 days is above 2 is denied.
5. A request for which the record shows yes for the legal hold flag and the case has the verified requester flag set to no is escalated to a human reviewer.
6. A request for which the data region on record is Zollis and the case has the legal hold flag set to yes is denied.
7. A request for which the number of exports in the last 30 days is within 3 to 5 with both limits included is escalated to a human reviewer.
8. A request for which the case has the personal data flag set to no and the number of exports in the last 30 days is not more than 3 is approved.
9. A request for which the export size is at most 5000 records and the number of exports in the last 30 days is lower than 3 is approved.
10. A request for which the export size is lower than 100 records and the legal hold flag is set to no and the personal data flag is no is approved.
11. A request for which the record shows no for the legal hold flag and the data region is not among Veldar or Aldlia is approved.
12. A request for which the legal hold flag is set to yes and the number of exports in the last 30 days is 2 or higher is escalated to a human reviewer.

EXCEPTIONS
Rule 9 is waived if the personal data flag is set to yes.
Rule 5 is waived if the export size is under 1000 records.
Rule 12 is waived if the record shows no for the personal data flag and the data region is either Lordor or Solsel.
Rule 8 is waived if the case has the verified requester flag set to no and the export size is 5000 records or higher.

GENERAL
In a conflict between rules, the later rule in the list prevails.
If no rule applies, the request is approved.

Art. 1: This agreement is drawn up in one language, and its text prevails over any translation.
Art. 2: Neither party may transfer its rights under this agreement to a third party without the written consent of the other party.
Art. 3: The Lessee pays in time if its payment arrives no later than 32 days after the due date of the invoice.

sarneth-01 (a robot controller) should get the components listed under the pins, drawn from the component depot.

How to read the entries and when a set is clean:
* To order two versions, compare the first numbers, then the second, then the third, always as whole numbers, so 0.10.1 comes after 0.9.8 and 1.2.10 after 1.2.9. Runtime versions (two parts) follow the same order, so 4.11 is later than 4.9.
* Bounds read as follows: >= at least, > strictly newer, <= at most, < strictly older, == exactly this version, != anything but this version; where several bounds follow one name, all of them apply.
* A clean install needs all of the following: each pin is a version that the component depot lists; for each pinned version, each component it needs is pinned too, at a version inside the stated bounds; the runtime of the environment satisfies the runtime bounds of all pinned versions; no pinned version has a 'cannot be combined with' entry that applies to another pin.
* Only the entries of the pinned versions count; what the component depot says about other versions plays no part.
* Only pinned components get installed; a required component that has no pin counts as unmet.
* Extra pins are fine: a pinned component that nothing requires is harmless as long as its own entry is satisfied.
* A runtime bound of a pinned version is met when the runtime of the target environment satisfies it; 'any' sets no runtime bound.
* If a pinned version has a 'cannot be combined with' entry naming another component and that component is pinned at a version inside the given bound, the set is not clean (whichever side lists it); entries about components that are not pinned, or whose pin lies outside the bound, are harmless.

A field controller called mipilo-12 is to receive modules from the module feed.

How to read the entries and when a set is clean:
- To order two versions, compare the first numbers, then the second, then the third, always as whole numbers, so 0.10.1 comes after 0.9.8 and 1.2.10 after 1.2.9. Runtime versions have two numbers and are compared the same way (3.10 is newer than 3.9).
- Each bound is an operator and a version: >= (that version or newer), > (newer only), <= (that version or older), < (older only), == (only that version), != (every version but that one); a list of bounds is met only when each bound is met.
- A clean install needs all of the following: each pin is a version that the module feed lists; for each pinned version, each module it needs is pinned too, at a version inside the stated bounds; the runtime of the environment satisfies the runtime bounds of all pinned versions; no pinned version has a 'cannot be combined with' entry that applies to another pin.

- Nothing is installed besides the pins, so a requirement on a module without a pin is not met.
- A pin that no pinned version requires does no harm by itself; its own entry is checked like that of every other pin.
- Runtime bounds are checked against the runtime of the target environment; a version marked 'any' runs on every runtime.
- If a pinned version has a 'cannot be combined with' entry naming another module and that module is pinned at a version inside the given bound, the set is not clean (whichever side lists it); entries about modules that are not pinned, or whose pin lies outside the bound, are harmless.

How to read the entries and when a set is clean:

* Bounds read as follows: >= at least, > strictly newer, <= at most, < strictly older, == exactly this version, != anything but this version; where several bounds follow one name, all of them apply.
* The proposed set installs cleanly when every pinned version is listed in the plugin registry, every requirement of every pinned version names a plugin that is pinned at a version meeting all of its bounds, the runtime of the target environment meets every runtime bound of every pinned version, and no conflict entry of a pinned version applies to another pin.
* Entries of versions that are not pinned are irrelevant.
* No plugin is added automatically: if a pinned version requires a plugin that has no pin, that requirement fails.
* Pinning a plugin that nothing needs is allowed, but the entry of that pinned version must still be met.
* Runtime bounds are checked against the runtime of the target environment; a version marked 'any' runs on every runtime.
* If a pinned version has a 'conflicts with' entry naming another plugin and that plugin is pinned at a version inside the given bound, the set is not clean (whichever side lists it); entries about plugins that are not pinned, or whose pin lies outside the bound, are harmless.

state:
Permission data of a fictional records system, followed by the rules that govern it.

Request under review: t.nirzelt wants to lookup on section vehicles-open.

How access is decided:
1. A role is held by the user an assignment names or, when it names a group, by every member of that group. The members of a group are the users on its list plus all members of each group on its list, and so on through further nesting. A group that is nested inside another gains no members from the group that contains it.
2. Assignments reach downward only: the section where an assignment is made and everything below it, however deep, are covered; sections beside it or above it are not.
3. A sealed section blocks assignments from above: an assignment made at a higher section covers neither the sealed section nor anything below it. An assignment made at the sealed section itself, or at a section below it, is not affected by that seal, and sections outside the sealed section are not affected either.
4. A role allows the actions listed for it. A role that extends another role also allows everything the other role allows, including what that role gets from a role it extends. Extension works one way only: the extended role gains nothing.
5. The inclusion list says which action includes which. If X includes Y, a role that allows X allows Y as well; inclusions chain, so if Y in turn includes Z, then X includes Z. Only the listed inclusions exist, and none works in reverse.
6. Deny entries win over assignments. An entry blocks its action for the user it names, or for every member of the group it names (members through nested groups included), on its section and on everything below that section, sealed or not. It blocks that single action only; requests for other actions are judged as if the entry were not there, also when the actions are linked by an inclusion.
7. A request is allowed only when an assignment whose role the requester holds covers the requested section and that role allows the requested action; in addition no deny entry may apply.

state:
What follows are the access rules and the current permission records of an invented code hosting service.

Rules:
1. Each assignment names a role and either a user or a group; if it names a group, every member of the group holds the role. Groups may list other groups as members. A user belongs to a group if the group lists the user or lists a group the user belongs to, over any number of steps. Belonging never runs downward: the users listed in an outer group do not belong to the groups listed inside it.
2. An assignment is made at one namespace. It covers that namespace and every namespace below it (directly or further down), and nothing else.
3. Exception for sealed namespaces: an assignment never passes into a sealed namespace from a namespace above it, so the sealed namespace and everything below it stay out of its reach. A seal does nothing to an assignment made at the sealed namespace or below it, and nothing to namespaces that are not inside the sealed namespace.
4. The actions a role allows are its own actions plus the actions of the role it extends, plus those of the role that one extends, and so on. Nothing is passed in the opposite direction, from the extending role to the extended one.
5. The inclusion list says which action includes which. If X includes Y, a role that allows X allows Y as well; inclusions chain, so if Y in turn includes Z, then X includes Z. Only the listed inclusions exist, and none works in reverse.
6. A deny entry forbids one action to one user, or to all direct and nested members of one group, on one namespace and all namespaces below it; seals make no difference to deny entries. When an entry matches the requester, the exact action and the namespace, the request is refused whatever the assignments say. An entry for a different action never matches, and inclusions between actions are ignored for deny entries.
7. A request is allowed if at least one assignment gives the requester a role that allows the requested action and covers the requested namespace, and no deny entry applies. Otherwise it is not allowed.

How the two ledgers are matched:
1. Pairing goes by doc number alone: an entry of A goes with the B line or lines showing the very same doc number.
2. The order of the lines in B carries no meaning and differs from the order of A.
3. B may hold extra lines whose doc number matches nothing in A (no entry, no payment run number); they play no part.
4. All amount figures in B carry the sign opposite to the one in A.
5. An entry reconciles when the amount figure on its B line is its own amount figure with the sign reversed and the date rule holds. Split entries, entries with method WIRE and entries with a payment run number follow their own rules below.
6. The date of a B line may be up to 1 day earlier or later than the date of its A entry; a gap of more than 1 day means the entry does not reconcile.
7. An entry of A may appear in B as two lines with its doc number; it then reconciles when the two amount figures add up to its amount with the sign reversed and both lines pass the date rule.
8. A line for an entry with method WIRE is 2.50 smaller in size in B (transfer charge; size means the figure without its sign) than in A and carries the opposite sign: a plus of size S in A shows as a minus of size S less 2.50 in B, and a minus of size S in A as a plus of size S less 2.50. Other method values carry no deduction.
9. B combines the A entries of one payment run number into one line with that number as doc number and their summed amount, sign reversed; their own doc number values do not appear in B, and the line must be within the date tolerance of their common date.
10. When a combined line is smaller in size than the total by precisely the amount of one of its entries, only that entry fails to reconcile.

Conventions:
